fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The writer says we have “…a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God…” The other high priests in this passage are appointed from among men. This one passed through the heavens.

Yes, baker, it's False. The writer says, “For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses…” So our high priest is able to sympathize. The writer goes on to say He “…was tempted in every way that we are…”
That's right, baker. The verse says He “…was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.” Every way, and still without sin. That little word “yet” carries a lot.

Riches would be nice, I won't lie. But the verse says we receive mercy and “…find grace to help us in our time of need.” What's offered is help for a time of need. Mercy is the word the writer picked.

A high priest leading the music, I like the picture, friend. But the verse says he is appointed “…to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.” Offering for sins is the heart of the job. The word is sacrifices.

Not quite, baker. God says, “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” That puts no end date on it, and it doesn't stop when His earthly life does. Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18).

That's right, it's False. The verse says, “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” Forever doesn't stop when His time on earth does. Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18).

Fasting doesn't come up in this verse, baker. The writer says Jesus offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears, and “…He was heard because of His reverence.” The reason given is His reverence, not something He did first. I think that's worth sitting with.
Preaching is a good guess, friend. But this verse says, “Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.” The word in the blank is suffered. Preached isn't in the sentence.

Built is an easy guess, baker, but the writer says Jesus “…learned obedience from what He suffered.” It's a surprising line, since He's called a Son in the same breath. I think it's a gentle reminder that He knows hard things firsthand. Suffered is the word that fills the blank.

Offering sacrifices is how the high priests do their work (Hebrews 5:1), friend, but that isn't the group this verse names. The writer says Jesus became the source of eternal salvation “…to all who obey Him”. Obeying Him is the answer.
